analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Amazon misses buyside; VMED looks to wholesale; CAP raises; UMG beats; INTEL guides below; ETL misses
key_insights: Amazon fell about 11% after hours. AWS grew 39.3% to $46.0bn, above sellside at 37.7% but below buyside at about 43%. AWS operating margin was 38.7% against the roughly 40% investors wanted.

Amazon group operating income was $28.1bn vs consensus $26.2bn. Advertising missed at $19.6bn vs Street $20.9bn. Q4 guidance top ends ($247bn revenue, $33.5bn operating income) were below buyside expectations and both midpoints were below Street.
Amazon cash capex of $75.9bn pushed trailing-12-month free cash flow to -$42.4bn, adding to the funding debate. Jassy projected AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028.

Hyperscaler read-through: AI demand is not the constraint, capacity and cost of delivery are. AWS $46.0bn (+39%), Azure $33.2bn, Google Cloud $30.7bn (+103%). Two hyperscalers flagged third-party AI chip/capacity delays pushing some capacity into 1H27, and Q3 capex came in light while full-year guides stayed elevated. The debate is shifting to how efficiently capacity is built and what return it earns.

Intel fell about 17% after hours. Q3 revenue and margins were in line to better, and DCAI revenue was $7.3bn (+78% y/y). Q4 guidance was well below the Street: revenue $15.5bn midpoint vs GS $18.0bn and Street $17.0bn, non-GAAP gross margin 38% vs Street 42.5%, non-GAAP EPS $0.25 vs Street $0.43. A PC slowdown is expected through at least 1H27 on memory price/availability and OEM inventory discipline.

Capgemini beat and raised. Q3 organic growth was 5.2% vs sellside 3.9%. FY organic growth guide rose to 4-4.5% from 3.5-4% (Street 4.1%). Operating margin (13.6-13.8%) and organic FCF (about €1.8-1.9bn) were unchanged. Book-to-bill of 89% compares with a normal 95-96%.

UMG results were far better than feared. Streaming subscription growth ex-downtown was 9.5% vs street about 8.5% and bears at 6-7%. Margin was 21.5%, 90bps above street. GIR nudged FY26+ revenue and adjusted EBITDA up by about 0-1%.
AI-generated music uploads rose from about 10,000 a day in Q1 2025 to almost 100,000 a day, per the UMG call.

BT rose 5% on an FT report that Virgin Media O2 is finalizing a wholesale deal to use BT's Openreach network (not confirmed) outside its footprint while freezing its own cable-to-fibre upgrades. VMO2 has £22bn of debt, bond prices fell sharply, and regulatory opposition to the £2bn Nexfibre transaction removed a planned £1.1bn cash injection.

Binance suspended withdrawals and pledged to cover losses after an attack affecting an estimated $6.3bn of funds. Polymarket halted trading on its international exchange after a third-party software provider was compromised.

Sandisk was unchanged after beating on revenue, gross margin and EPS. It announced an 8-for-1 split and bought back about $5bn of stock in the quarter. Q4 guidance of $12.4bn revenue and $55-57 EPS beat Street ($12.08bn, $52.94). The shares had fallen about 20% over 30 days.

ETL (Eutelsat) revenue missed by 4%, driven by an 8% miss in Video. Connectivity and Government were in line. Fixed connectivity missed as customers move from GEO to LEO, where ETL is subscale vs Starlink. FY targets were reiterated.

Proximus was mixed. Revenue and EBITDA were in line, domestic EBITDA missed by 1.8%, and lower capex produced an operating free cash flow beat. Strong Global performance led to upgraded FY guidance. Domestic EBITDA guidance of broadly stable was reiterated.
Twilio fell 15%. Q3 organic revenue grew 16% y/y, a slight slowdown from 17%, and the Q4 organic growth outlook disappointed. GS reads this as negative for Sinch.

STMicro: GS expects the Street to raise estimates by mid-single digits. Management said it is comfortable meeting Q1 revenue consensus within the 86-day quarter and saw no specific pull-forward in Q3 personal electronics. It is raising prices on selected products and sees stable to slightly higher pricing next year. Satellite revenue next year is expected to match or exceed this year's record, with capacity a constraint.

FCC proposal 26-71 would expand eligible spectrum for direct-to-smartphone satellite service from five to 13 bands (adding 482MHz) and allow local-area service or use of spectrum already licensed, easing waivers for Starlink and AST SpaceMobile.

Elisa: GIR sees a slower Finnish service-revenue recovery. Even the low end of FY26 telecom growth guidance of 0-2% is at risk, with modest downside to FY26/27 consensus growth of 0.3%/1.7%. GIR rating is Neutral, cut from Buy in September.

Telefónica: rivals urged the CNMC to reject its proposed five-year voluntary framework replacing cost-based duct and pole regulation, citing a cumulative 116% wholesale price rise. Telefónica puts the impact at €0.08-0.16 per line per month.

UK: VMO2 CEO Lutz Schueler called for a full investigation into BT's TalkTalk acquisition and criticised the CMA's two-week review deadline, arguing a regulatory double standard while the CMA challenges Nexfibre's Netomnia deal.

US trading desk: tech was weak (NDX -2.5%, AMZN about -10% after hours after -4% in the session) while S&P Equal Weight and cyclical/rate-sensitive stocks outperformed on a benign PCE. Consumer names caught a bid on covering in under-owned names (NCLH, CROX, BOOT), and CMG rose 8%. Floor activity was 5/10, asset managers were slight net sellers, hedge fund flows were about flat, and SPX volumes were +35% vs the 20-day average.

Derivatives desk: front-month QQQ fixed-strike vols were offered down about a vol at the lows and SPY vol fell more than 80 bps, as vol premium came out after tech prints. Skew was bid in SPX gamma tenors. A customer bought 15k SPX 31Mar 5500 puts as a crash hedge. The AI complex (GSTMTAIP -1.5%) was used as a funding source for everything else (SPXXAI +1.5%). S&P implied move through tomorrow is 0.70%.

Shares fell 15% on a disappointing Q4 organic growth outlook after 16% y/y organic growth in Q3.
Revenue, gross margin and EPS beat, Q4 guidance beat Street, and an 8-for-1 split was announced, but shares were unchanged after a roughly 20% decline over 30 days.
GS expects the Street to raise estimates by mid-single digits after management confirmed Q1 revenue consensus is achievable and flagged higher pricing.
Elisa was cut to Neutral from Buy by GIR in September, and slower Finnish service-revenue recovery puts the low end of FY26 guidance at risk.
Capgemini beat Q3 organic growth (5.2% vs sellside 3.9%) and raised FY organic growth guidance to 4-4.5%.

sector_views.rationale: Demand is strong and cloud growth accelerated, but capacity constraints, record capex and free cash flow pressure shift the debate to returns on investment.
VMO2 credit stress and a wholesale deal with Openreach help BT, while Finnish recovery at Elisa is slower than expected and Spanish duct regulation is under review.
Intel expects a PC slowdown through at least 1H27 on memory price/availability and OEM inventory discipline.

S&P implied move through tomorrow is 0.70%.
geopolitical: The FCC proposal 26-71 on direct-to-smartphone satellite spectrum has a political dimension in Europe, where governments need GEO providers such as Eutelsat as a counter to Starlink.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud growth accelerated (AWS +39% to $46.0bn, Google Cloud $30.7bn, up 103%), backlogs are substantial, and Amazon sees AWS growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Record capex, chip/power/data-centre constraints and capacity delays into 1H27 create free cash flow pressure, with Amazon trailing free cash flow at -$42.4bn.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AWS growth below the above-40% guide for 2027, or capacity delays extending beyond 1H27.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 organic growth of 5.2% beat sellside 3.9% and the FY organic growth guide was raised to 4-4.5%.
tension_points.bear_case: Book-to-bill was 89% vs a normal 95-96%, and margins and free cash flow guidance were unchanged.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Book-to-bill staying near 89% without a recovery toward the normal 95-96%.
